needs: tool gpg 3 | tool pass 1 | won plaintext_pixie | won cipher_crow
title: pass: a password store
summary: Keep each password in its own encrypted file, and let your scripts ask for it instead of writing it down.

text: pass keeps each password in its own file, encrypted with your gpg key (see the lesson on keys).
- The name is the path: backup/server is backup/server.gpg.
- Only your private key can open them.
$ pass init you@example.org      # once, with your key

scheme: $ pass generate web/shop 20  make a random one
text: - pass show decrypts one password and prints it. gpg may ask for your key's passphrase.
- pass generate makes a random one, so you never invent a weak one.
- pass -c name copies it to the clipboard instead of printing it.

scheme: DB_PASSWORD="$(pass show db/prod)"  ✔ at run time
text: A password written in a script is read by anyone who reads the script, and stays in its git history.
- $( ) runs pass when the script runs: the file never holds the password.
- A password that was ever committed must be changed: deleting the line isn't enough.
